items.note: K1.1/K1.2 state the lemma exactly and K1's method gives the eight-row cancel/use/restore structure and the three-stage composition. But the gate definitions, neighbour rules, the net change (JV+RG)x, the coefficient argument (|S∩T| mod 2 or (|S∩T|-1)/2, cancelled by the side wires) and the stage computation (x,y+x),(-y,y+x),(-y,x) are missing; K3.1 wrongly ties the cancellation to the label form.

The plan gives the common frame commuting with pointwise gates, the invariant, D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, all following lines 804-825. K2's own one-line summary drops S_Omega, but K2.2 restores it.

Present: nested nondegenerate labels in F^{⊗3}, <t_S,t_T>=|S∩T|-1, signed sum Wm-2N, only central 3->4 edges decreasing by h, L=Ich, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. Never written: the absolute sum Wm-2N+2L and dim F^{⊗3}=m. The derivation has no stage transitions, gate-label table or residual table, and no orthonormal-basis argument over F_2.

K3.5 states s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m and an endpoint difference I_m. It omits rho, which the identity needs: the difference is between sink(rho(w)) and source(w). It also omits the projection matrices P_U and -P_{U_a}, the shear frames Phi_M, and the conclusion that the network applies H<-H+D on every role. The rank-equals-dimension-change proof (P_V-P_U, the 2P_{U_a} source edges) is absent.

R3.1a states the one-kernel-per-orthonormal-residual-vector factorization and R3.1b gives C^{⊗e} on every role. The phase frames C_U=H^{⊗m}diag(i^{wt(P_U x)})H^{⊗m} are only alluded to as 'Hamming-weight phase frames'. The count s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m and the Z_{a,k}/i^{27k} endpoint corrections are missing, and the weight-additivity proof is not shown.

K3.4 gives L/N<1/2, K3.5 gives s_b<W_b m, and K4 gives s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}. This covers only the bit network: s_c<W_c m, sigma, the deficits eta_b and eta_c, and the argument eta>20·2^{-50}, log m<20 are absent ('large enough' only).

R1.1 lists the elementary scans and R1.2 the controlled shift, with the split-and-reorder mechanism of lines 577-580. R1.2's claim drops the b^{O(1)} offset-preparation condition (kept only in its quote) and the fixed rational-unit scalings that the triangular factors need. The elementary-stream proof is not shown.

Factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2, triangular parts as controlled shifts, and exactly a interchanges plus O(V): this is the paper's route. Two pieces are missing: the elimination proof of the factorization, and the gadget D_j<-D_j+H_i, swap, D_j<-H_i-D_j that turns each pivot into one interchange (named only as 'one pairwise swap'). The choice of the prime q is also omitted.

The plan has the row split into W role streams, edges as recursive interchanges, the three-shear interchange, s calls of volume V/W, the recurrence, the geometric sum and the depth-first schedule, as in the paper. Missing is the step showing that the network gives H<-H+D on every row: Phi_M frames, f'_{rho(w)}=Phi_{I_m}f_w, and the merge that undoes rho. The row-count divisibility by W^k is also omitted.

R2 states the lemma correctly and R2.2 sketches the route: rows from the chunks' high digits, remaining width in base m. Padding the row count to a multiple of W^k, padding binary ranges to [q^e], and the sum sum_j a_j m^{j tau}=O(e^tau) are not given.

The plan correctly gives the kernel factorization, s_c children on f=e/m axes, C^{⊗e} on every role, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. The conjugation by the binary basis change P_M, which puts residual directions into coordinate slots, is missing, and so is the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z C Z. The link to row additions appears only implicitly through R3.2/R3.3.

The eight conditional additions, the 80(f-1)2^{-K} bad fraction and the radix-sort repair match the paper. The cost O(V(L^tau+1)) is stated without the extra terms MA^3+delta_bad MA(R+A) and without the family hypotheses under which they vanish. The derivation omits the chunk swaps that bring the target after its controls, which are the source of L^tau, and the fact that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes B.

The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves F(e)=O(e) and the base-m partition are present. The condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda' is reduced to 'above the stated bounds', and q_0 as the row index is unexplained. The summation (K<=e^{c/beta} giving overhead e^lambda, a<=m^sigma, leaf term e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) is missing.

R3.5 states the proposition: Q_p(Hz), O(Vd^{lambda'}), error below sqrt2·2^{-p}. R3 assembles phase frames, packed moves, the recurrence and one final truncation, as the proof does. R3.4 asserts Delta=O(d^{C_1})=o(p) but not the arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E that bounds the guard width.

Character cancellation, DIF writing frequency j at rev_a(j), the procedures B_t F_t^- and F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, the layout (prefix moves O(TpdK), chunk exchanges O(Tp pK^{tau-1})) and the simultaneous rounds O(Tp l d^{lambda'}) all follow the paper. The grouped twiddle J_E is omitted but is not essential to the cost.
Packing at B_0=2^{4p}, centered residues using |h_j|<B_0/2, four exact products and the O(rp log(rp)) bound match the paper's proof.
The plan has the normalization identity, the retained LB order cancelling in the pointwise product, the error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, and the cost including O(Tp log(rp)), as in lines 3414-3495.

The one-dimensional identity, the approximation costs, the tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2, and the O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) line exposure are stated correctly. The construction of the Gaussian contractions A and B_0 (lines 3576-3792) is reduced to one phrase of method.

Both identities are stated, and R7b uses RF^+R=F^+ with permutations commuting with pointwise products, which is the paper's route. Missing: the chirp coefficient check, and the normalization step F_s(u*v)=S·F_s u·F_s v with F^+F=I/S that produces 1/S^2. The method's phrase 'dilations commute with transforms' is loose.

The sizes, the alpha choice, the prime interval and T/2<S<T are correct. The full fixed exponent list (tau, lambda, c, lambda', delta) and eta=1/(4d) are missing. The prime-count bound (Rosser-Schoenfeld), the Bernoulli estimate for S/T and alpha^4 theta_i>p are asserted, not derived.
Isomorphism, triangular coordinates and the controlled-shift implementation with its cost follow the paper's route.
The diagonal twist, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j and the convolution identity match lines 4303-4342.

The chirp and source transforms with exact counterpart RF_s, the five pipeline steps, and the two S factors undoing (u*v)/S^2 follow the paper. Omitted: the opposite procedure obtained by conjugation and the input scaling 2^{-b-2}, which is only implicit in 2^{2b+4}.

The chain E_s=9·2^gamma TL, then E_w<28·2^gamma T^2 L, then 448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2, then rounding and carries is correct. The ring and chirp bounds that feed E_s (5TL, 8TL) and the use of gamma<=b/4 are not shown.

The seven table rows, the margins, min g_i=2^{-181}=2kappa, the absorption of log p powers and the final O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}) bound all match the paper. Only the formula g_2=eps c(1-tau) is left implicit.
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n conjecture but gives neither the eventual-lower-bound formulation nor the liminf argument.

errors.says: The form gives <t_S,t_T>=|S∩T|-1, so neighbouring triples are orthogonal and unwanted gather/scatter coefficients can be cancelled by side wires.
errors.paper: The side-wire cancellation is a scalar coefficient computation in the proof of Lemma scalar-motifs: the central coefficient is |S∩T| mod 2, or (|S∩T|-1)/2 in the complex construction, and the side injection cancels it. It does not follow from the label form. The form <.,.>=x^T(I-J/9)y over Q is the bit network's label form, used only to make neighbouring triple lines orthogonal (lines 856-870); the complex labels use the F_2 dot product.

errors.says: Motivation: only the I central-wire return edges decrease.
errors.paper: There are Ic decreasing edges, c central wires per invocation over I invocations, each losing h, so L=Ich.

errors.says: The bit network's matrices differ by I_m between sink and source of every role.
errors.paper: The identity is M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m with rho exchanging X_a and Y_a. For role X_a itself, sink minus source is I+P_{U_a}; the identity holds only along the route X_a -> Y_a.

errors.says: Stored arrays carry frames that cancel between gates, so only the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1} is applied to each role.
errors.paper: The implemented operator is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and a route applies eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. Frames are not cancelled at gates; they persist as an invariant through each gate (K2.2/K2.3 state this correctly).

errors.says: The packed row addition costs O(V(L^tau+1)).
errors.paper: The bound is O(V(L^tau+1)+MA^3+delta_bad MA(R+A)). It reduces to O(V(L^tau+1)) only under the family hypotheses (A=O(p), R superpolynomial, K/log p->infinity).

errors.says: Method: dilations by units commute with transforms and with pointwise products.
errors.paper: Dilations intertwine with the transform as F_q^+ R_c = R_c^{-1} F_q^+, which gives RF_s^+R=F_s^+. They do not commute with it; only coordinate permutations commute with pointwise products.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from the bank-exchange network, frames, labels and matrix shears (K1-K6), through the butterfly layer (R3), transforms, convolution, resampling and assembly (R4-R8), to the final time accounting (R9), so it reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). The central saving thins at three points. The rational interface is asserted, not built: no projections P_U, no Phi_M frames, no link from the endpoint identity to H<-H+D on every role. The complex side never states s_c<W_c m. tau=1-2^{-50} is asserted without the eta>20·2^{-50}, log m<20 argument. Downstream, the layer recurrence's summation and the resampling construction are only stated.

steps.note: K1/K1.2 do give the fixed network exchanging the banks, (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), with every scratch wire restored. But h=100, the indexing of the data pairs by triples in T^3, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never given; N and m appear without definition. Conservative verdict.
Common frame commuting with pointwise gates, the operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and edge cost as a change of frame are all stated.
Nested nondegenerate subspaces of F^{⊗3} on every edge, with only the central 3->4 edges decreasing, each by h. The label dimension m is not stated.

K3's motivation asserts that an edge's cost equals its label's dimension change, and K3.5 mentions the 'extra N source ranks'. The mechanism (projections P_U, rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one) is absent.
The plan gives the signed sum Wm-2N, L=Ich, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b. The step adding 2L to get the absolute sum Wm-2N+2L is left implicit.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 below 1/2, hence s_b<W_b m. The deficit N-2L is implicit.

K3.5 gives an endpoint difference I_m without rho. Nothing says that, with frames Phi_M, the bit network therefore applies H<-H+D on every role. K5.3 only notes that the middle shear 'needs the network'.
Rank-a shear via E_1 Pi E_2 costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V), so a node makes s recursive calls in all.
Children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, F_k=O(e^tau). The justification eta>20·2^{-50}, log m<20 is reduced to 'large enough'.

central.summary: Six of nine steps are reconstructed: frames, labels, the budget, the strict saving, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence with its exponent. Three are only mentioned: the network's setup, without h=100, N or m; rank equals dimension change, without projections; and the endpoint identity, which is never turned into the shear H<-H+D on every role. So the plan conveys the counting behind s<Wm and the recursion that turns it into e^tau, but not how the label budget becomes the shear the recursion executes.
